title: Local roles: start a fresh session instead of compacting
lead: *Proposed.* Owner decision 2026-11-12 (relay session 8d711f67, chat: "2 is a great idea. file it"): a local role never reaches auto-compaction. When its context passes a threshold, ork ends the session and starts a new one with the same brief plus the role's own progress so far. A fresh start costs seconds; a compaction on the local server costs 15-19 minutes. Cloud roles do not change.
findings_note: S304 trial 2 (2026-11-12, S314): claude-local auto-compacted three times at about 83-86k tokens, taking 893 s, 983 s and 1121 s (50 of 90 min), and after the first compaction it lost its brief and went looking for it in its own transcript.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
*Proposed.* The local server spends 15-19 minutes per compaction because the model summarises the whole 85k-token context (trial 2 transcript `~/.claude/projects/-home-jon-code-squalor-xyz-ork--worktrees-S314/06e09bef-cc2f-4722-b1a3-4866518a6e48.jsonl`, `compact_boundary` entries). The work itself is not lost when a session ends: the edits are in the worktree. What a new session needs is the brief, the diff so far, and the role's short plan. claude CLI 2.1.322 has `--autocompact <auto|tokens>` with a 100k minimum, so compaction cannot be turned off below the launcher's window; ork must end the session first. ork already reads the claude stream (`internal/agent/claude/stream.go:152`); each assistant event carries the turn's input token count.

Open owner questions (the implementer asks them with `adj ask` first):

- Q1 (`roles.local-fresh-threshold`): at what context size does ork end the session? (a) *recommended*: 70k tokens, below the 83-86k where trial 2 compacted; (b) 60k; (c) a project setting with 70k as default.
- Q2 (`roles.local-progress-file`): where does the role keep its progress? (a) *recommended*: the role writes a short progress note (done, next, open problems) to `.scratch/progress-RUN-ROLE.md` in the main checkout after each step, and the new session's brief carries it with `git diff --stat` of the worktree; (b) no file: the new brief carries only `git diff --stat` and the diff of the changed files.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/agent/claude/stream.go:84-182` (per-turn input tokens)
- `internal/agent/claude/run.go:60-100`
- `internal/agent/claude/types.go`
- `internal/engine/round.go` (end and restart a local role's session within one round)
- `internal/engine/brief.go:65` (the restart brief: the brief plus progress)
- `internal/engine/watchdog.go:28` (the 90 min limit covers the whole round, across sessions)
- `docs/design.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A fake claude-local stream whose turn input passes the threshold is ended, and a new session starts without `--resume`, with a brief that holds the original brief, the progress note and `git diff --stat`.
- A cloud role passing the same size is not ended.
- The round's 90 minute limit counts both sessions.
- Each restart is recorded on the run (time and token count).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. `adj ask` Q1 and Q2 with `--ref` this slice; wait for the owner's answers.
2. Read per-turn input tokens from the stream, test first.
3. End and restart a local role's session per the answers; record each restart.
4. Docs (*proposed*): `docs/design.md`. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased`.
